newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rallies nine cts on pre-holiday buying.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rallies nine cts on pre-holiday buying.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed nine cents firmer on Thursday on a surge of short-covering ahead of the Easter weekend, brokers said.
May IPE Brent settled at $19.38 a barrel, seven cents off the high, after recovering from weakness seen around the NYMEX opening as traders squared positions before the long weekend.
"A lot of people didn't want to go home short. There was very good buying towards the close and this managed to edge out the sellers. It was a bit of a battle," a broker said.
The strenght of London buying helped narrow the Brent/WTI spread to around $1.25 from $1.45 earlier in the day, they said.
Brokers put May resistance at $19.50 and $19.61, with support at around Thursday's low of $19.20 and then at $18.83.
Uncertainty about Nigerian political unrest also helped the IPE contract to resist earlier NYMEX-inspired downward pressure.
A senior official at Nigeria National Petroleum Corp said that Shell could declare force majeure on early April cargoes if the unrest continued.
IPE gas oil futures closed down $5.75 on Thursday on technically-inspired selling. April settled at $166.75 after hitting a high in the morning of $169.75.
April heating oil was 0.37 cent stronger at 55.80 cents a gallon. Gasoline was 0.27 cent adrift at 64.55 cents a gallon.
